To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transcriptome of the African grass E. curvula is strongly influenced by ploidity, and that the expression of genes related to diplospory is strongly influenced by the genetic background.
the expression of genes related to polyploidy and diplospory was found to be altered in apomictic grasses.
we have identified a large number of differentially expressed transcripts in response to changes of ploidy and/or apomixis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of polyploidy and apomixis, which may have important implications for plant breeding.
the identification of genes involved in the regulation of ploidy, reproductive mode, and the transition from sexual to apomixis in the grasses.

the molecular mechanisms underlying the reproductive mode in E. curvula, and our results may be useful for the identification of candidate genes for polyploidy and apomixis in this grass species and in related genera.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of many genes in the Eragrostis genome is affected by ploidy and that the apomixis-associated region is a major target in the control of the reproductive mode.
ploidy is the most decisive factor in defining the transcriptomic structure of E. curvula.
polyploidy and reproductive mode (apomixis) affect the transcriptome structure in a tissue-specific and genotype-specific way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression profiles in the tetraploid sexual and apomictic plants are more similar than the diploid sexual ones.
the expression of genes related to ploidy, and possibly diplospory, is strongly influenced by ploidal level, and that the apomict has lost the expression of several genes related to diplospory.
the differential display analysis is an efficient tool to identify genes that show altered expressions in response to changes of ploidy and/or apomixis in the African grass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a differential display approach is a powerful tool for gene discovery, and that it may provide a useful alternative to microarray-based methods for gene discovery in polyploid and apomictic species.
a large number of genes are involved in the regulation of ploidy and/or apomixis.
the molecular basis for the apomixis and ploidy interactions is likely to be found in the genes identified in this study.
